scope: Replay of all 2916 documented objects (ordinary examples and keyword examples). A first full replay with the native build of integration commit a2a0038 (waves 5-7) found the regressions listed below; after a power cut destroyed its raw outputs, both replays were run again with the build carrying the regression fixes, and the objects whose examples call expand() were re-run with the final build (expand fix). Baseline for regressions: wave4-examples.json.gz overlaid by triage-wave4-final.json, and for keyword examples fifth-keyword-examples.json.gz overlaid by the later keyword batches.
reference_timeouts: SymPy timed out under load in keyword mode; symox completed every example, and the ordinary examples match
SymPy 1.14 needs 53 s for these examples on the loaded machine (load ~20); a direct SymPy run gives -2, -1, oo, [28, 35], Eq(f(x)/tan(f(x)/(2*x)), C1), identical to the symox outputs

regressions.cause: (Y**2)[10, 10] of a 1000x1000 FunctionMatrix materialised the whole explicit power (O(d**3)): 52 s, 21 s in wave 4
regressions.fix: MatrixExpr::element of a square of a lazy finite matrix multiplies one row by one column (SymPy MatMul._entry), then dotprodsimp as the explicit power; 0.5 s

regressions.cause: Predicate.__str__ uses _symox_predicate, which a BinaryRelation subclass does not set

gaunt(1000, 1000, 1200, 9, 3, -12): 93 s (SymPy 2 s, wave 4 6.5 s). Integer._eval_power (int_rational_pow, waves 5-7) calls perfect_power on huge factorial products, which tried an integer root for every prime exponent up to bits(n) (157 s for one sqrt)
regressions.fix: perfect_power follows SymPy's perfect_power(factor=True): trial division by small primes, a multiplicity 1 rules out every power, otherwise only divisors of the multiplicity are tried
